neighbour_prev_post_repair.strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening this unit at Ps.61.6 instead, isolating the dynastic material alone, was rejected because Ps.61.5's vow language is picked back up by the closing vow of Ps.61.8, so the two verses were kept as one bracketed movement.
observed_substrate_signals: (oshb:Ps.61.7) מֶ֣לֶךְ names “the king” (web:Ps.61.6) at the head of the dynastic material.

neighbour_next_post_repair.boundary_rationale: Past the psalm's refrain return at oshb:Ps.62.7 (= web:Ps.62.6), whose opening five tokens repeat oshb:Ps.62.3 byte-for-byte, this unit opens still in first-person voice, continuing the rock vocabulary of that refrain's close: “My salvation and my honor is with God. The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.” (web:Ps.62.7), where OSHB's צוּר עֻזִּ֥י (“rock of my strength”, oshb:Ps.62.8) echoes the refrain's own צ֭וּרִי. One verse in, register shifts to public exhortation: (oshb:Ps.62.9) בִּטְח֘וּ ב֤וֹ בְכָל עֵ֨ת עָ֗ם “Trust in him at all times, you people” (web:Ps.62.8), closing on the psalm’s second Selah. The unit moves through the wisdom reflection on human vanity, “men of low degree are just a breath” (web:Ps.62.9), and the warning against riches (web:Ps.62.10), closing on the revelatory formula (oshb:Ps.62.12) אַחַ֤ת דִּבֶּ֬ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים שְׁתַּֽיִם “God has spoken once; twice I have heard this” (web:Ps.62.11).
neighbour_next_post_repair.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Ps.62.7-62.8 as a continuation of the preceding confidence refrain rather than a fresh public-facing unit was rejected, given the shift from first-person soul-address to plural imperative address.
